name: Kemi
title: Kemi Ship Gauging: UTM at Ajos for Ice-Class Cargo Ships
description: Thickness measurement at Kemi's Ajos harbour: ice belt, bow, hold and tank gauging on forest-product carriers, container feeders and bulk ships in the north.
h1: Thickness Measurement for Ice-Going Ships at the Port of Kemi
intro: Kemi is the northernmost port on Finland's coast, at the top of the Bay of Bothnia close to the Swedish border. Its deep-water harbour at Ajos ships pulp, sawn timber and board from the Kemi mills and handles containers and general cargo, and ships here face one of the longest ice seasons in the Baltic. That makes the ice belt and bow the usual focus of gauging, alongside holds and tanks. Atlantis sends technicians from India for each Kemi job, timed to the ship's loading.

highlights.h: Ice belt wear at the top
highlights.p: Ships trading to Kemi spend weeks in the hardest ice the Baltic offers. Their ice belts, bow plating and shoulder frames take the most abrasion and impact, and spring is when owners want those areas measured before the summer docking.

highlights.h: Pulp and timber from Kemi's mills
highlights.p: Kemi's forest industry includes a large new bioproduct mill alongside sawmilling and board production. Ships loading pulp bales and timber at Ajos stay alongside long enough for hold, hatch and ballast-tank gauging between loading shifts.

Kemi is a short drive from Tornio and Haparanda on the Swedish border, and Bothnian shipping moves freely between the two coasts. A single mobilisation can cover ships at more than one port at the head of the bay in the same week.

port.h: Kemi, Ajos and the far-northern ice season
p: Kemi lies at the mouth of the Kemijoki, Finland's longest river, at the very top of the Bay of Bothnia. The town grew around sawmills and timber floated down the river, and forest industry still dominates its economy. The main cargo harbour is at Ajos, south of the town centre, a deep-water harbour with quays for containers, general cargo and bulk, and storage areas for forest products. A second harbour at Veitsiluoto serves the mill there. The approach from the open Bay of Bothnia runs through a dredged fairway across shallow water and a low, wooded coastline scattered with islands, and in the winter darkness navigation here relies heavily on icebreaker escort and on well-maintained fairway marking.

Traffic at Kemi reflects the north's industry. Pulp, sawn timber and board from the mills along the river and the coast go out by container and as general cargo, and the large bioproduct mill opened in recent years has added pulp volumes. The port also handles containers on feeder services and general cargo for the region's other industries. The ships are mostly small and medium short-sea types with Finnish-Swedish ice classes, because a large share of the calls fall in the ice season. Neighbouring Tornio, home to a large stainless steel works with its own harbour, makes this corner of the Bay of Bothnia an industrial cluster served by ships moving between Finnish and Swedish ports.

Ice sets the calendar at Kemi. The sea at the top of the Bay of Bothnia freezes early and thaws late, so ships need the higher Finnish-Swedish ice classes for much of the year, icebreakers escort traffic to and through the fairway, and the winter traffic restrictions for Kemi stay in force for a long part of the year. In summer the same waters are calm and the nights short and light, which is when most ships dock and when owners prefer to do planned survey work. Even the town's tourist trade has an ice theme, with a retired state icebreaker taking visitors out into the frozen bay from Ajos each winter. A Kemi gauging job usually follows a seasonal logic, before the freeze or after the thaw.

Ajos is where nearly all our Kemi work takes place. Forest-product carriers and general cargo ships load over a day or more, and their holds can be measured before loading starts, with ballast tanks and the ice belt from inside done during the loading itself. Container feeders work faster, so their scope is split across calls: ice-belt framing and plating from inside the forward tanks on one visit, decks and the remaining tanks on the next. In winter the outer shell at the berth is often surrounded by broken ice, so external readings wait for the open season.

Kemi is not a docking port for merchant ships in our planning, and owners dock the ships that trade here at repair yards elsewhere in Finland, in Sweden or in the southern Baltic. What Kemi provides is the first look at the winter damage. A spring call, after the ice has gone, lets the team measure the ice belt, bow and shoulder plating and the frames behind them, so the yard can be told the steel quantity before the ship arrives. Work at anchor is not part of the plan here.
list: Ajos container quay — feeder ships on fixed rotations; staged gauging of forward tanks, ice belt and decks over consecutive calls
Ajos general cargo and forest-product berths — pulp and timber carriers; hold, hatch cover and ballast-tank gauging before and during loading
Ajos bulk berths — dry-bulk ships; hold and tank-top readings as holds are cleared
Veitsiluoto mill harbour — ships serving the forest industry; gauging fitted into the mill's loading programme

context.h: Ice class, inspection and northern trading conditions
p: Port state control at Kemi is carried out by Traficom as a member of the Paris MoU, and an inspector boarding a ship that trades to the top of the Bay of Bothnia will look closely at the ice belt, the forepeak and the frames behind them, because that is where winter shows. Under the Finnish-Swedish Ice Class Rules, ice-belt plating and framing are sized for the ice class, with a margin for abrasion and corrosion built in, and when wastage eats into that margin the ship's notation, and with it her eligibility for icebreaker assistance into Kemi, comes into question. Ice class hull gauging at Kemi is therefore about keeping a ship's trading licence for this port.

Forest-product receivers expect pulp and timber delivered dry and undamaged, so ships loading at Kemi need weathertight hatches and holds free from leaks through corroded boundaries with the ballast tanks. Much of the tonnage serving this corner of the Baltic is ice-class short-sea ships that owners keep in service for many years, and older ships carry wider renewal-survey scopes and need condition checks between surveys. Feeder services between Kemi and hub ports elsewhere in the EU run legs that fall under the EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime, and ships arriving from outside the EU carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation.

jobs.p: Kemi work is shaped by the ice more than anything else. The biggest single category is the spring check, when owners want the ice belt, bow and frames measured after a winter's trading, closely followed by the autumn check before ships commit to winter contracts. Forest-product carriers bring hold and hatch cover gauging tied to cargo condition, container feeders bring survey preparation split across their calls, and occasional ice-damage incidents bring short-notice requests for shell and frame measurements and crack detection. Each scope is fitted around the loading programme at Ajos and agreed with the chief officer before the team boards.
list: Post-winter ice-belt, bow and shoulder plating gauging on an ice-class general cargo ship at Ajos, feeding the summer docking steel list
Pre-winter gauging of ice-belt plating and frames on a container feeder, so the owner knows her class margin before the traffic restrictions tighten
Hold and hatch cover gauging on a pulp carrier after receivers reported wet cargo
Shell and frame measurements with magnetic particle crack detection after an ice-damage report in the Bay of Bothnia
Renewal-survey preparation on a feeder ship spread over several Kemi calls

logistics: Kemi-Tornio Airport, close to Kemi, is served from Helsinki, and the airports at Rovaniemi and Oulu are alternatives by road when flights are full or disrupted. Our technicians come from India on Schengen visas, which also cover the short trip into Sweden if a ship at a Swedish port is added to the same mobilisation. The ship's agent arranges access to Ajos, and the forest-industry harbour has its own site rules. In winter we plan for cold, darkness and possible delays to flights and icebreaker escort.

faqs.q: What does an ice-belt gauging scope cover on a Kemi ship?
faqs.a: It covers ice-belt shell plating over the waterline region set by the ice class, the bow and shoulder areas, and the frames, stringers and brackets behind them, measured from inside wherever tanks and spaces can be entered. We record local thinning around dents and abrasion, compare readings with the original scantlings and the class margin, and add magnetic particle checks on frame connections where damage is suspected.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ship at Kemi in the middle of winter?
faqs.a: Inside, yes: holds and tanks are measured as at any other time once spaces are ventilated and warm enough to work in, using couplant suitable for sub-zero conditions. Outside, ice packed against the hull limits shell readings at the berth, and arrival times depend on icebreaker escort. For external shell scopes we suggest the open-water season; internal survey preparation can go ahead in winter.

faqs.q: Can one trip cover ships at Kemi and across the border in Sweden?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Kemi is close to the Swedish border, and Finland and Sweden are both in the Schengen area, so the same visa covers both countries. If ships in a fleet are due at Kemi and at a Swedish Bothnian port such as Luleå in the same week, we plan one mobilisation and sequence the jobs around their port calls.

faqs.q: Where do ships trading to Kemi go for docking?
faqs.a: Owners choose repair yards elsewhere in Finland, in Sweden or further south in the Baltic, usually in the summer when the ships are not needed for ice trading. We help by measuring the ship at Kemi first, so the yard receives an ice-belt and tank steel list it can plan around, and the same team can verify bottom and shell readings once the ship is dry.
